Former Synagogue in Georgensgmünd

Former Synagogue · Georgensgmünd, Germany

The synagogue in Georgensgmünd was built between 1733 and 1735 on land acquired at the edge of the village, replacing earlier informal prayer rooms used by the local Jewish community. The sandstone building contains two ritual baths (mikvahs) and retains wall paintings attributed to the itinerant Baroque painter Elieser Sussmann. The Jewish community, once nearly 40 percent of the village's population in the 17th century, dwindled under Nazi persecution; the last Jewish residents were forced to leave in 1938. The municipality purchased the building in 1988 and restored it with support from the district; it now functions as a museum and cultural venue, part of a complete ensemble with the adjacent Jewish cemetery.
